reader_summary.headline: Gavin Baker explains why AI fundamentals are accelerating despite recent stock market drops.
reader_summary.overview: Gavin Baker argues that AI companies are actually growing faster than the market realizes. He points out that metrics like GPU usage and token growth are accelerating, even as stock prices fall. He also highlights that big tech firms are not cutting spending and that demand for computing power remains extremely high.

key_points.text: Fundamental data for AI companies like GPU usage and token growth is actually accelerating despite recent market drops.
key_points.evidence_quote: Loads of AI names are down 50, 60% from their highs. We'll call it 40 to 60% in a month and a straight line. And I asked you before we started, you've been out here for the summer, have you heard a single negative quantitative metric about AI? A single instance of deceleration. Nothing. Nothing. In fact, every metric is accelerating.

key_points.text: Big tech companies like Meta are not cutting spending on new chips, even though the stock price fell recently.
key_points.evidence_quote: And this is seen as like very bearish. They have excess capacity. They're going to cut CapEx. This is a disaster. This is not at all what it was. They just supported. They didn't cut CapEx.

key_points.text: Prices for renting computing power are rising sharply instead of falling, showing that demand is much higher than supply.
key_points.evidence_quote: They're renting the exact same size cluster. Essentially identical in every way, B200 said no differences. And they're hoping seven months later to pay just under four dollars. Today, like, that's pretty crazy.

key_points.text: Memory is the most important factor for increasing AI output and lowering costs because it works directly with compute power.
key_points.evidence_quote: It's the single most important thing you could do to increase token output per unit of compute. And then that obviously definitely actually lowers costs

key_points.text: Open source models allow companies to build unique AI solutions at lower costs, helping new businesses grow quickly.
key_points.evidence_quote: And it's also a godsend for all these AI natives. You know, it's like our friend Vishriya, I think he said two years ago, I've never seen more companies go from being founded to like $50 million a year in revenue
